subject: community-medicine
title: Live and Killed Vaccines, Cold Chain, VVM, Shake Test and Open Vial Policy

steps.title: Live vaccines multiply in the host
steps.tx: **Live attenuated vaccines** contain organisms passaged until they lost disease-causing power while keeping immunogenicity: BCG, oral polio, measles and yellow fever. They multiply in the host, so the antigenic dose grows beyond the injection, all major and minor antigens engage, and one dose usually protects. Immunodeficiency and pregnancy contraindicate most of them.
steps.say: Living vaccines keep working after injection. Attenuated organisms multiply, antigen dose grows, every component engages, and one dose usually protects. Immune deficiency and pregnancy forbid most of them; that pairing fills exam stems.

steps.title: Killed vaccines: safer, weaker, repeated
steps.tx: **Inactivated vaccines** are grown then killed by heat or formalin: injectable polio, hepatitis A, rabies and whole-cell pertussis among them. They cannot multiply or revert, so they suit the immunocompromised, but they generally protect less strongly and need multiple doses plus boosters. Cholera vaccine's roughly 50 percent protection is the classic efficacy warning.
steps.say: Killed products trade power for safety. No multiplication, no reversion, safe in immune deficiency, but weaker and hungrier for repeat doses. Cholera vaccine near fifty percent protection is the classic warning figure.

steps.title: Subunits, toxoids and conjugates
steps.tx: **Subunit vaccines** present selected antigens: toxoids (tetanus, diphtheria), protein and recombinant vaccines (hepatitis B), polysaccharide vaccines, and conjugates that link polysaccharide to protein so infants respond, as in Hib and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines. Adjuvants such as aluminium salts amplify response where the antigen alone is weak.
steps.say: Selected antigens form the third family. Toxoids, recombinant hepatitis B protein, plain polysaccharides, and conjugates that recruit infant responses. Aluminium adjuvants amplify weak antigens. Platform decides age suitability, dose count and cold chain behaviour.

steps.title: The cold chain end to end
steps.tx: The **cold chain** holds vaccines between +2 and +8 degrees Celsius from manufacturer to beneficiary through walk-in freezers and coolers, deep freezers, ice-lined refrigerators, cold boxes, vaccine carriers and conditioned ice packs. Breaks accumulate invisibly: potency lost to heat never returns on re-cooling, which is why monitoring, not trust, guards every link.
steps.say: Two to eight degrees, factory to arm. Walk-in stores, deep freezers, ice-lined refrigerators, cold boxes, carriers and conditioned ice packs form the relay. Heat damage accumulates invisibly and never reverses on re-cooling.

steps.title: Heat sensitivity has an order
steps.tx: **Heat sensitivity** ranks vaccines for storage discipline: oral polio vaccine is among the most heat-labile, while tetanus toxoid and hepatitis B tolerate heat better but freeze easily. Ice-lined refrigerators hold the +2 to +8 range at primary facilities; deep freezers make ice packs and store only what freezing cannot harm. Light also damages BCG and measles vaccines.
steps.say: Sensitivity has a ranking. Oral polio vaccine fears heat most; tetanus and hepatitis B fear freezing instead. Ice-lined refrigerators hold the working range, deep freezers serve ice packs, and light itself damages BCG and measles products.

steps.title: Vaccine vial monitor reads cumulative heat
steps.tx: A **vaccine vial monitor** is a heat-sensitive label whose inner square darkens with cumulative heat exposure: lighter than the outer circle means use the vaccine, equal colour means use it first, darker means discard. Types VVM2, 7, 14 and 30 reach discard in that many days at a constant 37 degrees. It never detects freezing.
steps.say: One label remembers every warm hour. Inner square lighter than the ring: use it. Equal: use it first. Darker: discard. The number counts days to discard at thirty seven degrees. Freezing leaves no trace here.

steps.tx: A **vaccine vial monitor** is a heat sensitive label whose inner square darkens with cumulative heat. Lighter than the outer circle means the vaccine may be used. Colour equal to the circle means that vial should be used first. Darker than the circle means discard. Types VVM2, VVM7, VVM14, and VVM30 reach discard after that many days at a constant 37 degrees. The square remembers warmth. It never detects freezing, so a vial that has frozen can still display a square that looks usable.
steps.say: The inner square of a vaccine vial monitor darkens as heat adds up. Lighter than the outer circle means use the vial, the same colour means use it first, and darker means discard. The type number is how many days at 37 degrees bring the discard point. Freezing leaves no mark on this label.

vis.alt: Three vaccine vial monitors show an inner square lighter than, equal to, and darker than the outer circle.
vis.caption: The inner square progresses from paler than the reference ring, to the same colour, to darker than the ring as heat exposure accumulates. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Shake test for suspected freezing
steps.tx: The **shake test** checks freeze damage in adsorbed vaccines: freeze a same-batch control vial solid at minus 20 degrees overnight, thaw, shake both vials vigorously for 10 to 15 seconds, rest 30 minutes and compare sedimentation. Faster or equal sedimentation in the test vial means freeze damage and discard; slower means the batch survives.
steps.say: Freezing betrays itself by settling. Freeze a same-batch control overnight, shake both together, rest half an hour. Test vial settling as fast as the frozen control means damage and discard; slower settling clears the batch.

steps.tx: The **shake test** checks freeze damage in adsorbed vaccines. Freeze a same batch control solid overnight at minus 20 degrees, then thaw it. Shake both vials hard for 10 to 15 seconds and let them stand for 30 minutes. If the test vial sediments as fast as the frozen control, or faster, the batch was frozen and is discarded. Slower sedimentation means freezing has not ruined it and the vaccine may still be used.
steps.say: Freeze a same batch control solid overnight at minus 20 degrees, thaw it, and shake it with the suspect vial for 10 to 15 seconds. After 30 minutes, settling as fast as that frozen control means damage and discard. Slower settling means the batch survived freezing.

vis.alt: Two vials rest after shaking, one sedimenting slowly and a frozen control sedimenting quickly.
vis.caption: After a timed rest, the test vial stays cloudy longer while the deliberately frozen control has already settled. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Open vial policy: 28 days, with exclusions
steps.tx: The **open vial policy** lets opened multidose vials of DPT, TT, hepatitis B, OPV, liquid pentavalent, PCV and injectable IPV be reused across sessions for up to 4 weeks (28 days) if expiry, cold chain, aseptic technique, uncontaminated septum and VVM all pass. Measles, MR, BCG, JE and rotavirus vials are excluded and discarded, BCG and measles within 48 hours.
steps.say: Opened vials need not die daily. Named liquid vaccines serve up to twenty eight days across sessions when expiry, cold chain, asepsis, septum and monitor all pass. Reconstituted measles, BCG and JE vials stay excluded and perish fast.

right.title: Never reused
points: Discard within 48 hours or session end

steps.title: Two live vaccines: spacing rule
steps.tx: When two **live vaccines** are not given on the same day at different sites, at least 3 weeks (commonly taught as 4 weeks) must separate them, so the first vaccine's interferon response cannot blunt the second. The same visit remains best practice. Measles vaccine seroconverts 95 to 98 percent after one dose; the second dose exists to catch the remainder, not to boost.
steps.say: Live pairs need choreography. Same day at different sites, or weeks apart, so early interferon cannot blunt the second vaccine. Measles converts ninety five to ninety eight percent first time; dose two catches the remainder rather than boosting.

rows: Separate by at least 3 to 4 weeks
